title: Clarify/fix helper.derive docs
body:
Trying to use a derived helper, a couple of things got me hung up [from the docs](https://community.algolia.com/algoliasearch-helper-js/reference.html#derive-multi-queries).

I wanted my derived helper to search on a new index. The `helper.derive` function states `The signature of the function is SearchParameters -> SearchParameters`. However, there is no mention in the docs of a `setIndex` method for `SearchParameters` (though it seems to work, and [what I need to use](https://github.com/algolia/algoliasearch-helper-js/issues/337#issue-169108447)).

Furthermore, the docs refer it firing the `results` event, when it should be `result`. PR here: https://github.com/algolia/algoliasearch-helper-js/pull/476

comments.body: My bad, I need to rework the doc and make the SearchParameters more exhaustively documented. Thanks for reporting!

np, thanks.
I've managed to grind through it now, but an example of a multi-index query w/ `.derive` in the docs would be excellent.
@timkelty any chance you can share your solution? I'm also starting to look at using this feature, and as you mention the documentation is a little sparse.
@thomo13 let me know if there is something that you don't understand, that would be of great help :)

Well at the risk of sounding somewhat stupid I'm not even sure if this can help me to accomplish what I want to do. 

Basically I have some fairly large docs, so to keep the size under control I'm using ID fields in one index to reference documents in a different index. 

One of my users has just requested a filter on indexA based on the status of a related item in indexB. I'm not sure if this is something the derive function can help with, I was hoping for an example of some kind so that I might wrap my head around how it works.

Thanks both for your replies.... I guess ultimately this isn't what I was looking for, but interesting nonetheless 

I guess my options are 1) replicate the information across the indexes or 2) make two requests and use a disjunctive facet to filter the final result set...
@thomo13 Feel free to drop a comment / request for feedback on your use case directly in the [algolia community forum](https://discourse.algolia.com) :) Lots of helpful people around there :)

Struggled to find some docs too, glad for this issue honestly :)

Hope this will make it to the official docs and examples some day soon.

Ultimately advanced features of the helper like derive aren't encouraged as we will have a more straightforward way of debugging if it's done using InstantSearch. For that reason we won't add more documentation.
